questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code routes operations to shards? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The cluster grows from 8 to 9 shards. Why is Guava's consistentHash used instead of Math.floorMod(hash, shardCount)?
choices: It produces a better spread of keys across shards than modulo hashing
Only about one ninth of keys move to a different shard, whereas modulo would remap most of them
It makes shard lookups possible without knowing the shard count
It guarantees that no tenant is ever larger than another

questions.prompt: During searchAll, shard 5 times out while the others respond. What does the caller receive?
choices: A failed future, because allOf fails if any call fails
Results from the other shards with partial = true
Results from the other shards, indistinguishable from a complete answer
An empty result, because merging requires every shard

questions.prompt: What is the main operational cost of routing by tenantId rather than by docId?
choices: Tenant-scoped searches must be sent to every shard
Documents of a very large tenant all land on one shard, which can become a hot or oversized shard
The router has to be rebuilt every time a tenant is added
Document ids can no longer be unique within the index
